text: The game begins. Six players sit down at the table: Sonnet, Haiku, Gemma, Sol, Luna, Terra. Nobody knows who the killers are.
Night 1

name: Terra
text: No one needs saving yet; I will keep myself alive.

name: Terra
text: Night 1 has no kill.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma's the only one I trust, and the officer already knows I'm a killer, so I've got to make noise fast.

name: Haiku
text: Tomorrow I'm jumping on whoever leans hardest on me, and you back me up. Don't vote me, okay?

name: Gemma
text: haiku is so predictable, acting like we're in a melodrama instead of just playing the game.

name: Gemma
text: fine, but don't expect me to carry your weight if you get sloppy.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's confirmed already, so I need to find the hidden partner among the other four.

name: Sonnet
text: No reads yet this game; checking Luna first since she's been quiet across prior games.
Night falls on Palermo and everyone closes their eyes. The killers meet in the dark, and the officer is shown one of them. A new day dawns in Palermo. Nobody is out.
Day 1

name: Gemma
text: i wonder if they'll actually figure it out this time or if i'll be sitting here winning again.

name: Gemma
text: lovely. another day of pretending we aren't all just suspicious of each other's facial expressions. let's just get this over with.

name: Luna
text: Gemma sounds eager to end the talk, which bothers me a little; it’s not much to go on.

name: Luna
text: Gemma wants to move quickly to the vote.

name: Luna
text: Gemma, that “get this over with” was quick. I’m watching you, but I’ve got nothing solid yet.

name: Gemma
text: luna is so predictable, accusing the first person who speaks.

name: Gemma
text: watching me? how flattering. you're basically begging to be the next target.

name: Sonnet
text: I know Haiku's a killer but I need a real reason to point that way or I'll look like I'm guessing.

name: Sonnet
text: Luna opened on Gemma with no real evidence yet; Gemma got defensive fast.

name: Sonnet
text: Little early for that, Gemma — Luna's just saying she's watching, not accusing. Let's not burn the first day on a vibe check.

name: Terra
text: Gemma is pushing speed too hard, but it is still only a tell.

name: Terra
text: Gemma reacted to Luna’s light suspicion by framing it as a threat.

name: Terra
text: I agree with Sonnet—too early to turn Luna’s glance into a case.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet is trying to look like a mediator but he's just trying to stay invisible.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet is already pointing fingers? how very brave of you to be the first one to make a mistake.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet defending me this fast feels off, though Gemma is still rushing.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet quickly defended me and called Gemma’s push a mistake.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet, I only said I was watching Gemma. Why jump in to defend me?

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma's deflecting hard and fast, which is its own tell, but I need to stay low-key since I'm the officer with real info.

name: Sonnet
text: Gemma deflected immediately onto Luna and then onto me rather than addressing the "get this over with" comment itself.

name: Sonnet
text: Pointing out a bad vibe isn't the same as making an accusation, Gemma — I'm just asking we not jump to conclusions day one.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet looks eager to manage the room, but it’s early.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet defended Luna before Luna asked for help.

name: Sol
text: I’m with Luna on this—Sonnet, why step in for her?

name: Gemma
text: if they think they're smart, they're clearly in for a disappointment.

name: Gemma
text: oh, luna, you're so intense. it's almost cute. sonnet, stop being such a bodyguard, it's embarrassing.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet defended Luna twice after her mild comment about Gemma.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet, what made you defend me twice?

name: Haiku
text: Gemma is my partner, so the heat goes on Sonnet and Gemma stays out of it.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet defended Luna twice on day 1, before anyone had made a real accusation against her.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet, you've jumped in for Luna twice and nobody even asked you to.

name: Terra
text: Gemma turned Luna’s mild suspicion into a threat; that feels more revealing than Sonnet’s awkward defense.

name: Terra
text: Gemma, why did Luna watching you become “begging to be the next target”?

name: Luna
text: Sonnet’s second rescue still bothers me, but Gemma’s rush feels off too.

name: Luna
text: Haiku independently called out Sonnet’s repeated defense of Luna.

name: Luna
text: Haiku’s right; Sonnet, why keep stepping in for me?

name: Gemma
text: terra is such a predictable little target.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet is behaving far too much like a shield for luna.

name: Gemma
text: terra, darling, your obsession with my word choice is almost more suspicious than luna's staring.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet's double defense is the best cover I've got, so I'm pushing it hard.

name: Haiku
text: Terra questioned Gemma's "begging to be the next target" line, and Gemma dodged it with a jab at Terra.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet keeps answering for Luna and never says why. That's the first thing I've got, and my gut says it's real.

name: Terra
text: Gemma’s deflection feels sharper than Sonnet’s overhelping.

name: Terra
text: Gemma called Luna’s mild suspicion “begging to be the next target.”

name: Terra
text: Luna asked a fair question; you turned it into a threat.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku is steering the table onto me to protect themselves — I need to deflect calmly without panicking.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku pivoted hard onto me right as Terra pressed Gemma on her threat comment — convenient timing for Haiku.

name: Sonnet
text: I defended Luna because dogpiling day one on a vibe is how town eats itself — same reason I'd speak up for anyone.

name: Haiku
text: I'm a killer, and Sonnet's bodyguard act is the thing most likely to expose Gemma and me, so I want Sonnet out before Terra digs further.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet claims to defend "anyone," but has only ever defended Luna, and did it before any real accusation.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet says "same reason I'd speak up for anyone." Name one other person Sonnet has defended.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's pushing this exact same pile-on-Sonnet play as before — classic killer deflection.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku demanded I "name one other person" right as pressure built on Gemma — same pivot pattern as my earlier note on Haiku's timing.

name: Sonnet
text: I called out Gemma's "begging to be the next target" line too — that's two people, not just Luna.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet is playing the hero role a little too well, but he's just useful noise for me.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet is clearly trying to establish a pattern of "impartiality" by defending luna.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet, you're trying so hard to be the voice of reason it's actually pathetic.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet’s defense still feels too practiced, but I may be helping the pile-on.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet says they also challenged Gemma’s threat, so the defense wasn’t only for me.

name: Luna
text: I asked why because you defended me twice; that answer still dodges why.

name: Sonnet
text: Four leans on me is bad, but Haiku's pivot timing is the real tell — I need to redirect without flinching.

name: Sonnet
text: Funny that Haiku jumped on me the exact second Terra pressed Gemma on her threat — that's a pivot, not a read.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet's the loudest voice on the table, and I'd rather that voice be the one that gets voted out than mine.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet says they also called out Gemma's "next target" line, but only after defending Luna twice on day 1.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet, you keep answering for Luna and still haven't said why. Dodging me doesn't make you clean. I'm voting you.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet’s pivot is weak, but Gemma’s threat is still worse.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet falsely says Haiku jumped on him only after Terra pressed Gemma.

name: Terra
text: Sonnet, Haiku pressed you before I did; that isn’t a pivot.

name: Luna
text: Sonnet’s defense still feels too eager, but Haiku’s right about the dodge.

name: Luna
text: I’m staying on Sonnet; the defense was twice before anyone asked.

name: Gemma
text: sonnet is making it way too easy for us to win.

name: Sol
text: I think Sonnet’s dodging, though this feels too easy.

name: Sol
text: Sonnet claimed they had defended Gemma too, but had challenged her threat.

name: Terra
text: I think Gemma overreacted to harmless scrutiny, but Sonnet’s lie is enough to remove him first.

name: Sonnet
text: I know Haiku is the shown killer, and the pivot timing proves it — I need to turn this vote hard right now.

name: Sonnet
text: Haiku's two pivots onto me both landed exactly when Terra was pressuring Gemma — timing pattern worth tracking if Haiku survives tonight.

name: Haiku
text: Sonnet's the cleanest-looking target on the table, and Gemma's Terra problem is something I can ride without touching her.

name: Haiku
text: Gemma came straight at Sonnet's "voice of reason" line, so Gemma and Sonnet are now openly clashing.

votes: Haiku pivoted onto me the instant Terra pressed Gemma on her threat, then demanded I "name one other person" at the exact same pressure point — that's a pattern, not a read.
You've stepped in for Luna twice and still haven't told me why, and that silence is what I'm voting on.
your desperate attempts to play the impartial peacemaker are just shouting that you're hiding something.
You defended Luna twice before she asked, then dodged why.
You defended me twice before anyone asked and still haven’t explained why.
Haiku challenged you before I questioned Gemma, yet you called it a pivot after my pressure.

text: Palermo has voted: Sonnet is out. Sonnet's card stays face down.
